newsitem.title: SWEDEN: FORECAST - Swedish CPI seen up 0.2 pct in February.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - Swedish CPI seen up 0.2 pct in February.

text.p: Sweden's consumer price index (CPI) is expected to have risen 0.2 percent in February month-on-month and to show no rise year-on-year, according to a Reuter poll of 15 economists.
Forecasts range between 0.1 percent and 0.4 percent for the monthly rise and from a fall of 0.1 percent to a rise of 0.2 over 12 months.
For the full 1997 year, economists expect the CPI to rise 1.0 percent. Consumer prices rose on average 0.7 percent in 1996 from 1995.
In January 1997, consumer prices rose 0.1 percent from December 1996, and fell 0.1 percent year-on-year.
In February 1996, CPI rose 0.1 percent on the month and 1.7 percent over 12 months.
Statistics Sweden will release February CPI March 12 at 0815 GMT.

Economists interviewed came from Carnegie, Consensus, Den Danske Bank, Deutsche Morgan Grenfell, Hagstromer & Qviberg, Handelsbanken, HSBC Midland, JP Morgan, Merrill Lynch, Nomura, Nordbanken, Paine Webber, S-E-Banken, Sparbanken, and Unibank.
